summary: Smoke test of the freshly cloned VisaXpert app. Backend: 10/10 pytest pass (GET /api/ shows 'VisaXpert API' with status running, /api/health shows DB connected, POST /api/webhook/lead for website/university_change/ielts_celebration/germany_fair/media_design_webinar, POST /api/enquiry, dashboard login ok/401, stats, leads search (each new lead shows up in the list), public reviews/partner-logos/success-stories/page-logos/uc-appointment-toggle). Frontend: homepage hero form submits (POST /api/webhook/lead returns 200 and the success state shows); /study-abroad, /berlin, /germany-fair, /ielts-celebration, /countries, /branches, /contact, /faq, /webinar/media-design, /privacy-policy, /terms, /impressum all render with no JS page errors; /university-change redirects to /berlin; the Berlin UC form submits and shows the 'Thank you!' message; dashboard login with the admin account works and the submitted UI leads appear in the table with the right sources (homepage, university_change). The third-party channels without keys (Resend/Sheets/FB) skip without breaking the request.

minor.issue: The AiSensy WhatsApp API keys (AISENSY_API_KEY and AISENSY_API_KEY_UC) are hardcoded in server.py lines 44-46, so WhatsApp sends are really attempted against the live AiSensy account. They currently fail with 'No Plan active on assistant!' and are logged, and the request still succeeds. Risk: real WhatsApp messages would go to test phone numbers if that plan becomes active.

action_items: Optional: move the hardcoded AiSensy keys in server.py into backend/.env when the user supplies third-party keys.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 5445 lines; a monolith (as-is from the repo, not changed in a smoke run).
Hardcoded AiSensy JWT keys in source (server.py:44-46).

Dashboard auth sends the email and password as query params on every request (e.g. /api/dashboard/leads?email=&password=), which exposes credentials in logs and URLs. This is the repo's original design.
Unreachable code after the return in get_dashboard_stats (server.py:2877-2891).
seed_data_creation: TEST_-prefixed leads were created during testing and then deleted from the leads collection (the DB now has 0 leads).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Smoke suite: /app/backend/tests/test_smoke_clone.py. The Berlin form selectors are form-name, form-email, form-phone, form-transfer-type, form-submit and uc-success-message. The home form uses hero-form-* selectors. Dashboard login uses login-email, login-password and login-submit. Avoid page.expect_response in long browser scripts: a combined script hung the harness once (it was a tool artifact, not the app).
